subject: acc-dy
title: ACC.DY.------INFO.F.
description: Diagram closing R(AS)CM(II)-50 — the section transitioning into the Decentralization argument. The prose immediately above identifies the structural object: 'the relationship between creative musicians and their community must be viewed as important.' The crossing diagrams what accent-dynamics meets when it tries to reach the form-of-information that musician-community relationship would carry: ACC-DY (accent dynamics — what creative-music's accenting actually does in working terms) is crossed with INFO-F (information form — the actual form that accent-dynamics' information takes when received). ACC-DY sits on the left with the subject-arrow; MTA-RT-SIGN (meta-reality signal) hangs to its left as the subject's leftward output, with LG-DY (linguistic dynamics) anchoring the lower-left margin and LANG (language, written as 'lang.d.' for language-definition) and MOT-DY (motion dynamics) centrally as the subject's downward hub. AFI-1 (affinity insight, level one) rises above the subject as the upper bridging hub, with TR (transformation) at the upper-right. INFO-F sits as partner-axis at center-right; SPT-DY (spectacle dynamics) rises at right and HI-P (high purpose) sits on the right margin, with INDIV-DY (individual dynamics) at the lower-right as the partner-side's downward output. Structural argument: when accent-dynamics is crossed with information-form, the upper diagonal AFI-1 → TR is the load-bearing edge — affinity-insight is what carries accent-dynamics into transformation as actual information-form. The subject's leftward chain MTA-RT-SIGN → LG-DY is what accent-dynamics produces on its own as meta-reality signaling; this is real but unhoused. The partner's HI-P → INDIV-DY chain shows where information-form lands without the upper diagonal — high-purpose individual-dynamics, the isolated artist the prose-section critiques (the next Decentralization argument names that those who 'were not born or raised in New York... were instead forced to migrate as a means to make a living'). The diagonal must hold or the community-musician relationship the section names cannot route the form's actual accenting into its receiving community.
